Subject: Inquiry: per-tenant TTL + EU storage for PII

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. As we evaluate Redwood for production, a couple of compliance questions came up from our security team. High level: we need (a) per-tenant configurable TTLs so our legal team can set shorter retention for EU customers, and (b) firm guarantees that data for EU tenants is stored in EU regions and can be purged on-demand.

Can you confirm whether those are currently supported or on the roadmap? If not, can you share a rough target timeline and what evidence you can provide (audit logs, deletion confirmation hooks, proof of deletion)? I'm compiling a short SOW for procurement and would appreciate any details.

Attaching a data map that shows which data categories are considered PII for our use case.

Best,
Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and the data map. Looping in Karthik (eng) and Grace (product) to confirm specifics and next steps.

Short answer: we support model-level regional routing today and we have per-tenant metadata hooks, but we do not yet ship a self-serve per-tenant TTL configuration UI. We do have internal APIs that can apply retention rules per-tenant and a recent prototype for on-demand purge API.

Karthik / Grace — can you weigh in on current capabilities, what’s production-ready, and a feasible timeline to expose per-tenant TTL + guaranteed region pinning for EU tenants? Also, what deletion proofs (audit events, s3 object lifecycle confirmations, or cryptographic deletion receipts) can we provide to customers as compliance evidence?

Elena — I put a short follow-up ask below that will help us scope the SOW. Would you be able to share expected per-tenant retention buckets (e.g., 30/90/365 days), typical volume per tenant, and whether legal requires immediate rollback/restore windows after deletion?

Thanks,
Monica Patel

Thanks for the ping. Quick engineering notes:

- Regional routing: we have region-aware placement for model inference and can pin a tenant to an EU cluster; this is already in production for a handful of enterprise tenants.
- TTL controls: storage layer supports object lifecycle rules at the bucket level today. We have an internal service that maps tenant IDs to lifecycle policies, but there is no customer-exposed control plane for per-tenant TTLs yet.
- On-demand purge: prototype exists (purge API that removes KV cache + associated storage objects, emits deletion audit events). Need to validate for multi-region replication and dependent caches (e.g., embeddings cache).
- Evidence: we can emit deletion audit events (with object keys) and provide S3 delete markers / lifecycle logs. For guaranteed cryptographic proof, we need to scope work; we can provide signed deletion attestations as an engineering deliverable if required.

Open questions for scope (please answer so we can estimate):
1) Do you need UI-level controls or will an API + SOW be sufficient?
2) Volume: average tokens and storage size per EU tenant (helps estimate retention cost).
3) RPO/RTO expectations around purge (is immediate soft-delete acceptable, or do you need hard-delete confirmation within X hours?)

Proposed timeline (high level): 8–12 weeks to expose per-tenant TTL API and on-demand purge with audit logs for EU-only tenants, plus 2–4 additional weeks if cryptographic deletion attestations are required.

I'll follow up with a short tech spec and Jira ticket.

- Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Folks — adding product perspective and a proposed customer-facing minimum viable scope so we can align procurement/SOW expectations.

MVP for FinSecure (customer-facing):
- Per-tenant TTL API (tenant-level metadata): allow retention values of 30 / 90 / 365 / custom (in days). API should validate and return a retention policy id.
- Region pinning: tenant->region binding for read and write that guarantees EU residency for data at rest and for backups.
- On-demand purge API: synchronous request returns a deletion job id; job completes within SLA and emits audit events with object ids.
- Evidence bundle: downloadable zip with audit event log, storage delete markers, and a signed statement (PDU) from Redwood indicating deletion job completion.

Constraints / notes for SOW:
- Multi-region replication complicates immediate hard-delete; for MVP we will guarantee removal from primary EU region and queued deletion in replicas. SLA for full propagation: 48 hours.
- Cost: retention beyond 90 days will be quoted separately; include a retention surcharge in the SOW.

Timeline suggestion for external commit: 10 weeks from sign-off to API availability (includes 2 weeks QA + 1 week docs + 1 week for evidence bundle plumbing). If customer accepts API + SOW (no UI), we can deliver faster.

Rachel — can you draft the SOW outline and add the retention surcharge examples? Monica — let's get the required retention bucket sizes from Elena and confirm the procurement cadence.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Security & Compliance

Hi Monica, Grace, Karthik — thanks for the thorough responses. A few clarifications from our side:

- Retention buckets: we expect 30, 90, and 365 days as standard buckets; a custom option is required for legal exceptions (rare).
- Evidence expectations: audit logs + storage delete markers are sufficient for now; cryptographic attestations are nice-to-have but not mandatory for the initial contract.
- Propagation: 48-hour propagation window is acceptable, but we need a hard SLA in the SOW for EU tenants.
- UI vs API: procurement prefers an API + SOW to start; a UI would be helpful later but not required.

I've attached the data map and added an internal note about our expected number of EU tenants (approx 12) and estimated monthly storage of ~200GB across those tenants.

Next step for us is to receive a short SOW draft and a proposed timeline so we can start internal approval.

Best,
